title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
source: canonical Maximum Depth of Binary Tree concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is the root node of a binary tree; each node holds a value and points to a left and a right child, either of which may be absent. Return the number of levels in the tree: a single node has depth 1 and an empty tree has depth 0. The TreeNode class is provided in the starter code.
constraints: the tree stays balanced enough that recursion is safe

examples.explanation: The levels hold 5; then 3 and 8; then 1, 7, and 9.
A single node makes one level.

hints: The depth of a tree is one more than the deeper of its two subtrees.
Every node belongs to exactly one root-to-leaf path, so one full walk can measure them all.
Walk with a stack carrying (node, depth): track the deepest depth seen and push children one level deeper.
solution: One traversal carrying each node’s depth: the answer is the deepest depth seen. O(n) time, O(depth) stack space.
failureHint: hidden tests include an empty tree, a single node, and a lopsided tree

visible.failNote: a single node sits at depth 1
